title: A person's deliberate block on u9h was silently dropped by the run's own merge, which keeps dispatching the attempts the block exists to stop (fifth counterexample)
body: At 18:41 local the session lead committed 1b725f49 (origin/main): tick 37i created and "37i" added to u9h's blocked_by, so the run 'stops cycling on it and stops spending interventions'. At 18:43 the run's merge 96977e99 (origin/main into epic/dha, parents 3c706e57 and 1b725f49) resolved .tick/issues/u9h.json byte-identical to the run side — git diff 3c706e57..96977e99 on that file is empty — deleting the "37i" entry the person had just added, while the SAME merge added .tick/issues/37i.json itself: half the person's commit landed and the block link was silently reverted. The claim and the tick-graph read that admitted u9h both happened before the merge, so the block was never visible to the orchestrator, which dispatched attempts 22, 23, 24, 25 AND 26 against the person's recorded intent — five counterexamples, each spending the go6 interventions the block exists to prevent, with attempts 24's and 25's reports explicitly saying 'do not dispatch the next attempt' before each dispatch. The shape: a file the run rewrites (.tick/issues/<tick>.json) receives a human edit on main, and the run's merge resolution takes its own side verbatim, so any person's governance edit to a live tick is silently reverted while a run is mid-claim; a merge that drops a blocked_by entry added by a non-run author must fail loudly rather than resolve, and the tick-graph read that gates dispatch must see the merged result including such blocks. Still unfixed and still untriaged at attempt 26.
